moduleTitle: Lesson 2 - Create and Register records through TDS
learningObjectives: Use TestData - Create & provide new item to add test data to a TDS type.
Explain what an Alias name is, when it defaults, and when it must be used.
Distinguish Find reservation from non-locking ReadOnly access.
Generate multiple test records at once using the Repetitions setting on an Execution Entry.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Creating records with a TDS Standard Module

elements.description: Use TestData - Create & provide new item from the Standard subset's Test Data Management → Test Data Service folder to add an item to an existing or new type. Security-enabled installations may restrict access by user group.
Specify Existing or new TDS type and define the needed attributes under Data structure with ActionMode Input. Supply an alias when later operations need to identify this item.

bulletPoints: Create adds one item with the configured attributes; reuse its alias in the same TestCase.

elements.description: An alias identifies an item available during the TestCase; it is not a repository column or a search condition. The documented Find workflow uses the type name as the default when its alias is omitted. Use an explicit alias for later update, move or delete operations.

Independent example: find sender and recipient items using appropriate selection criteria, then assign distinct aliases so subsequent steps address each known item. An alias alone does not choose the correct role or replace those criteria.

elements.text: Do not infer which aliases an inaccessible Academy exercise used; the example here is independent and uses explicit aliases.

elements.description: Check both selection and identity: Find criteria determine the intended item; its alias addresses the retrieved item in later steps. A default type-name alias is not the name of its first attribute.

bulletPoints: Blank Alias name → defaults to the TDS type name, not an Attribute name.
Use distinct aliases to address different known items within one TestCase.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Viewing records and understanding the lock

elements.description: Use Test Data Management to inspect the intended repository, type and item attributes. Its lock controls indicate reservation; a manually locked item is not editable in the Web UI. Interface colors and layout may vary with the installed version.

elements.text: Find reserves the retrieved item. Automatic release is documented after execution or a new loop iteration, including failure. ReadOnly does not acquire that lock; explicit release is a separate operation.

elements.description: Create an item of type CustomerDetails with alias customer. Set a synthetic Email and Status = New using Input. These are example attributes, not a built-in customer schema or a verified Academy registration walkthrough.

elements.text: For repeated execution, link the configured TestCase in an ExecutionList and inspect results for each run. No Tosca execution has been performed as part of this editorial example.

elements.description: Set the ExecutionEntry's Repetitions property to run its TestCase multiple times with the same values. If each successful run creates one item, five successful runs add five items. Repetitions alone does not generate unique data or guarantee successful creation; check each result.

bulletPoints: ExecutionEntry Repetitions repeats the TestCase; a TestStep folder's Repetition property repeats its contained steps.

elements.text: 📄 Exercise 02A-02D (Register Test Records through TDS, View Test Records in Test Data Management, Register a Customer in the Web Shop, Create Multiple Customers) — Official Tricentis Academy course material, not redistributed here. Access it inside the official course.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming a blank Alias name inherits an Attribute's name
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Believing an empty Alias name field takes on the name of whichever Attribute is being referenced.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: In the documented Find workflow, an omitted alias defaults to the type name, not an attribute.

examPitfalls.title: Skipping Alias name when one TDS type serves two roles
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Storing both a bank transaction's sender and recipient under the same 'CustomerDetails' type without an Alias to tell them apart.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Select the intended role's item using criteria, then assign a distinct alias; alias naming does not replace selection.

examPitfalls.title: Expecting a retrieved record to stay available to other testers
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming a colleague can immediately reuse a record you just retrieved, while your TestCase is still running.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Find reserves an item; ReadOnly does not. Verify the intended ownership and release path for your test.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A tester leaves Alias name blank in TestData - Find & provide item for type CustomerDetails. What default alias does the documented Find workflow use?

options.text: It takes the name of the first Attribute entered.
It takes the name of the TDS type — 'CustomerDetails'.
Tosca always rejects a Find with a blank alias.

practiceQuiz.hint: The Find default comes from Existing TDS type.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The documented Find example uses the type name when Alias name is omitted.

optionExplanations.A: An attribute name is not the documented default resource alias.
optionExplanations.B: The default is Existing TDS type, here CustomerDetails.
optionExplanations.C: Tosca uses the type-name default to address the retrieved item.
optionExplanations.D: The documented Find example deliberately leaves the alias blank.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A bank transaction test needs to store both a sender and a recipient, both under the TDS type 'CustomerDetails'. What should the tester do to avoid a TestCase pulling the wrong role's data?

options.text: Select each intended item with suitable criteria and assign distinct aliases for later steps.
Leave Alias name blank for both.

practiceQuiz.hint: Selection chooses the data; aliases identify known items for subsequent operations.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Distinct aliases let later steps address each selected item without confusing their roles. The aliases do not themselves filter the repository.

optionExplanations.A: TDS cannot infer these business roles from a shared type name.
optionExplanations.B: Selection criteria identify the right items and distinct aliases address them later.
optionExplanations.C: Separate repositories are unnecessary merely to reference two known items.
optionExplanations.D: A shared type-name default does not give the two roles distinct references.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A TestCase creates one item per successful run. Which setting repeats its ExecutionEntry ten times without copying its TestSteps?

options.text: Set the ExecutionEntry's Repetitions property to 10.

practiceQuiz.hint: There's a dedicated setting on the Execution Entry for exactly this purpose.
practiceQuiz.rationale: ExecutionEntry Repetitions runs its TestCase multiple times. Ten successful runs each creating one item produce ten items; the property does not guarantee success or uniqueness.

optionExplanations.A: Copying steps changes the TestCase rather than configuring repeated ExecutionEntry runs.
optionExplanations.B: Repetitions is the documented ExecutionEntry property for repeated runs.
optionExplanations.C: An alias is an item reference, not an execution counter.
optionExplanations.D: ExecutionEntry repetitions are supported in the documented execution workflow.

quickRecap.value: TestData - Create & provide new item: type, optional data structure, explicit alias for later operations.
Selects/creates the type the record is stored under.
Blank → takes the TDS type's name (not an Attribute's).
Criteria choose the intended item; its alias addresses it in subsequent TestCase steps.
Find reserves its retrieved item; release occurs after execution or a new loop iteration, including failure. ReadOnly is non-locking.
ExecutionEntry Repetitions repeats runs; verify each creation result and design unique values when needed.
